name: Notion
summary: Notion has two paths. A public integration has a short self-serve form with no review. The hosted MCP server supports Dynamic Client Registration, so an agent can register its own OAuth client without a developer account.

verdict.label: Easy
verdict.headline: Public integration in 10 minutes with no review. Via MCP, an agent can register an OAuth client by itself.

approvalWait.appliesWhen: never; the Notion integration gallery listing is optional

agent: Register an OAuth client on mcp.notion.com/register via DCR (no developer account)
Run the PKCE flow against mcp.notion.com/authorize
Prepare the public integration form fields
human: Sign in to Notion and approve the consent screen (choose which pages to share)
For a classic public integration: create it in the integrations dashboard and copy the secret

steps.title: Pick a path: MCP (DCR) or classic public integration
steps.detail: MCP: the agent calls Notion's hosted MCP tools, and the OAuth client is created on the fly. Classic: you get REST API access with a fixed client_id/secret that you own.

steps.title: MCP path: register a client via DCR
steps.detail: POST client metadata (redirect_uris, client_name) to the registration endpoint and receive a client_id. No account is needed for this step.

evidence.note: Discovery doc at mcp.notion.com lists registration_endpoint and S256 PKCE

steps.title: Classic path: create a public integration
steps.detail: notion.so/profile/integrations → New integration → type Public. Fill in redirect URIs, company name, website, privacy policy and terms URLs.

steps.title: User consents and picks pages
steps.detail: Notion's consent screen makes the user select which pages and databases to share. The agent only sees what was shared.

requirements.note: Required on the public integration form.
Some workspaces restrict who can add integrations.

evidence.note: Based on admin settings; not verified

endpoints.tokenLifetime: Not documented for classic public integrations

evidence.note: MCP discovery: registration_endpoint present, PKCE S256. api.notion.com has no discovery doc (400)

blockers.symptom: API returns 404 for a page that exists
blockers.cause: The user didn't share that page with the integration during consent.
blockers.fix: Re-run consent or have the user add the integration via the page's ••• → Connections menu.

gotchas.title: No scopes, only page-level sharing
gotchas.detail: Notion doesn't use OAuth scopes. Access is whatever the user selects, so agents should handle 'not shared' gracefully.

gotchas.title: DCR clients are per-agent, not per-brand
gotchas.detail: The consent screen shows the client_name you registered. You don't get the same control over branding as with a classic integration.

tested.result: 400, no discovery for the classic API

uncertainties: We didn't POST to /register to avoid creating a stray client; the DCR claim comes from published metadata.
